messages:
Dan (AcmeHealth): Hey team — during the ramp test just now we saw ~20% 503s starting around 10:12am PT. This is the POC traffic (burst to 5k rps). We're blocked on verifying SLA. Can someone triage?
DeployBot: ALERT: 503 spike detected on cluster poc-acme-01 — queue_depth=820, scale_event=triggered at 10:12:15 PT
Alex (Eng): thanks — can you paste a failing request id and the model you're hitting? also was this against Hosted or Dedicated POC pool?
Dan (AcmeHealth): Hosted POC pool, model=redwood-7b, example request id: req_3f9b2a. Rapid ramp from our load test runner. Sample curl: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"hello"}'
# response snippet:
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"error":"service_unavailable","msg":"busy, try again"}
```
Mira (Infra): looking at infra metrics — backlog spiked and autoscaler started new instances but there was a ~45s cold-start gap. Our current autoscale cooldown for hosted-pooled customers is 60s which lets backlog grow in aggressive ramps. Also seeing high KV cache miss rate leading to longer per-request latency.
Chen (Eng-Infra): Investigation notes: the burst_pool for this POC was set to 40 instances. At 5k rps with concurrency ~8 we exceed effective capacity. I pushed a temporary bump to burst_pool=140 for this customer in the test env (will revert). Also lowered max_concurrency_per_instance from 8->4 to reduce queueing.
Alex (Eng): good call. Two quick mitigations: 1) increase burst pool for the POC run, 2) enable automatic failover to quantized variant redwood-7b-int8 when queue_depth>500. We have a routing policy flag we can set per-customer.
Dan (AcmeHealth): If you flip to int8 for failovers, will output quality drop? We need to show correctness to our stakeholders.
Mira (Infra): int8 has slight variance on edge cases but for our demo prompts it's within acceptance. We can run quick evals before the next ramp to verify.
Jamie (Sales): On billing — for the POC week we don't charge customers for incomplete/errored generations (we refund token charges on 5xx). There is nominal infra cost exposure on our side; if you need guaranteed throughput we can propose a short reserved capacity commitment for the demo window and produce a pricing add-on.
Sara (AM): Also flagging security/compliance Q from Acme: they asked about log retention and customer access. For hosted POC we can restrict request logs retention to 7 days and scrub payloads; alternative is Private/VPC with customer-managed KMS which removes us from access. Dan, would you like a Private eval?
Dan (AcmeHealth): For the POC we were hoping to stay hosted but with tightened retention. Private might be a blocker for timeline. 7 days looks ok for now.
Alex (Eng): SDK behavior note: client SDK retries 2x with exponential backoff on 5xx but does not auto-switch models. We can wire a server-side routing policy to route retries to the int8 variant on sustained 5xx for this customer. That will happen before SDK retries to avoid double attempts.
Chen (Eng-Infra): I applied the routing policy to the POC tag (route_on_5xx->redwood-7b-int8 after 3 consecutive failures). Also enabled additional tracing for req_3f9b2a-similar to capture KV cache misses.
Dan (AcmeHealth): Appreciate it. One more Q: will those automatic failovers affect SLA reporting? Stakeholders want accurate error numbers.
Jamie (Sales): Failovers count as successful edges in availability metrics if the request completes with a 2xx after routing. We'll provide a separate breakdown (primary vs fallback) in the console for the POC so you can report raw 5xx incidents vs routed completions.
Mira (Infra): Action items for next ramp: increase burst_pool -> 140, max_concurrency_per_instance -> 4, enable route_on_5xx to int8, monitor queue_depth, and shorten autoscale cooldown for this customer to 20s for the test window.
Dan (AcmeHealth): Can we run another ramp tomorrow at 10am PT with those changes? Also please share the short security note for retention so I can reply to procurement.
Sara (AM): I'll DM the sec note and add a short agreement about 7-day retention for the POC.
Alex (Eng): Logged followup ticket INFRA-7891 to revert burst_pool post-POC and to make the routing policy ephemeral for this customer.
Dan (AcmeHealth): Great — thanks everyone. We'll run at 10am PT tomorrow and ping this channel if anything pops.
DeployBot: RESOLVED: spike mitigations applied (burst_pool bump, routing policy) at 10:20:45 PT
